source_text:
Ἀδιαλείπτως οὖν προσκαρτερῶμεν τῇ ἐλπίδι ἡμῶν καὶ τῷ ἀρραβῶνι τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἡμῶν, ὅς ἐστι Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς, ὃς ἀνήνεγκεν ἡμῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας τῷ ἰδίῳ σώματι ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον, ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν, οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ: ἀλλὰ δἰ ἡμᾶς, ἵνα ζήσωμεν ἐν αὐτῷ, πάντα ὑπέμεινεν.
μιμηταὶ οὖν γενώμεθα τῆς ὑπομονῆς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐὰν πάσχωμεν διὰ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, δοξάζωμεν αὐτόν. τοῦτον γὰρ ἡμῖν τὸν ὑπογραμμὸν ἔθηκε δἰ ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ἡμεῖς τοῦτο ἐπιστεύσαμεν.
orientation: Polycarp is opening his letter by urging the Philippians to hold fast to Christ, who bore their sins and endured all things so that they might live in him.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore let us continually persist in our hope and in the pledge of our righteousness, who is Christ Jesus, who carried up our sins in his own body onto the tree, who did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth; but for our sake, so that we might live in him, he endured all things. Therefore let us become imitators of his endurance, and if we suffer for the sake of his name, let us glorify him. For he set this example before us through himself, and we believed this.

lemmas.gloss: let us persist in, hold fast to

choices.why: The glossary fixes this term as 'pledge' for the guarantee of their righteousness, which is Christ.
The verb means to bear or carry up; 'carried up' preserves the upward motion of offering sins on the cross.
The literal word is 'tree' or 'wood'; 'tree' keeps the biblical idiom for the cross without interpretive gloss.
The glossary fixes this term as 'example' for the pattern of Christ's suffering.
The glossary fixes this term as 'endurance' for patient suffering modeled by Christ.

bible_refs.note: ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν, οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ

pass_b_english: So let us hold fast without ceasing to our hope and to the pledge of our righteousness, who is Christ Jesus. He carried up our sins in his own body to the tree. He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth (Isaiah 53:9). Yet for our sake, so that we might live in him, he endured everything.
Let us then become imitators of his endurance, and if we suffer for his name, let us glorify him. For he set this example before us through himself, and we have believed it.

problems.source_quote: ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν, οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ
problems.why: The quotation is from Isaiah 53:9 (LXX), not 1 Peter 2:22. While 1 Peter 2:22 quotes Isaiah, Polycarp cites the prophetic source directly.
problems.ruling: Source quotes Isaiah 53:9 LXX directly; citing 1 Peter 2:22 misleads readers about the scriptural reference Polycarp uses.

edits.old: He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth (1 Peter 2:22).
edits.new: He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth (Isaiah 53:9).
